quotes.text: The hearing today, I think, is one that is very timely. We find ourselves in a moment of great uncertainty. You could call it a tale of two virtual realities. Some people are afraid we’re going to have a Star Trek moment; some people are afraid it’s going to be the terminator.

The impact of AI will have on cognitive development, and learning is not well understood, and some experts are sounding the alarm that cognitive skills are being negatively affected. The guidelines about what safe and ethical AI should look like in the classroom are not well defined and vary greatly from place to place, yet reports show that 84% of high school students are using generative AI for schoolwork.
We want people to be able to take advantage of the benefits of AI, but also be protected when using it.

As the founder and co-chair of the bipartisan Future of Work Caucus in Congress, I commend @POTUS on this EO that will help us both mitigate the challenges and seize the opportunities posed by AI - especially when it comes to our workforce and economy. https://t.co/JSgMhVo5X6

Artificial Intelligence presents incredible opportunities and unique challenges.

That's why I introduced the bipartisan AI Literacy Act with @RepLarryBucshon to ensure that AI is at the heart of digital literacy programs so we can mitigate its risks and harness its potential. https://t.co/mGpQs20hkR

I’m grateful to have hosted a conversation today with my Future of Work Caucus co-chair @RepGarbarino to hear from experts about how we can harness emerging technologies like artificial intelligence to help solve workforce challenges facing the health care system. https://t.co/yRmgVUOQBT

We must be prepared for the evolving technology of the future.

That's why I founded the Bipartisan Future of Work caucus and introduced the AI Literacy Act.

Our workforce must be prepared - for the sake of our economy and our futures.

https://t.co/kZGZZ4aaOR

AI presents us with incredible opportunities along with unique challenges.

Today, on National AI Literacy Day, we must recommit to ensuring that we can not only mitigate the risk of AI, but seize the opportunity it creates. Let's start by passing my bipartisan AI Literacy Act!

I am in awe of @RepWexton’s resilience. I encourage everyone to take a moment to watch this video. The potential of AI is immense and this is an important example of how it can be used for for good. https://t.co/rDhTzk85fK

To enhance consumer awareness and confidence in the use of AI by directing the Department of Commerce to develop a national strategy to increase consumer knowledge, create use case guidance, and disseminate guidance and information through a national media campaign.

Today, I introduced the bipartisan Consumers LEARN AI Act, legislation that will empower Americans with AI literacy.

This bill will give people the knowledge and confidence they need to use this technology when it can be helpful and avoid it when it could be harmful. https://t.co/ee0EZJ2kZH

It is imperative that the United States establish a clear and robust path forward on artificial intelligence that positions our nation as the winner in the AI race. From a national security and domestic policy perspective, the federal government must be forceful in investing in AI and scaling the necessary infrastructure to compete and innovate. Though I believe the Executive Branch should play a role in providing clarity on a path forward, I do not believe that we should allow culture wars and deep partisanship to shroud the ability of states and Congress to regulate this rapidly evolving industry. What’s more, any responsible AI policy framework must prioritize the environment, and should focus on resource protection and energy efficiency technologies.
The United States cannot afford to lose the global AI race, but any path forward must be through strong, thoughtful leadership and value innovation, the environment, and national security.

As Delaware’s former Secretary of Labor and the Ranking Member of the Education and the American Family Subcommittee, I have long been dedicated to ensuring our students leave the classroom with the skills and knowledge they need to succeed in our changing economy. It is clear that understanding AI will be imperative to that success. This important piece of legislation will empower states to develop academic standards on AI and prepare our leaders of tomorrow to meet the moment.

Our kids need to be AI-literate.

They need to know the problems, the protections, and the possibilities. https://t.co/Td7ToqKVSS

As AI continues to disrupt our economy, it’s absolutely essential we protect workers and lay the groundwork for future success.

Proud to be leading proactive legislation with @maziehirono and @SenAdamSchiff to make sure innovation and supporting our workforce go hand in hand. https://t.co/PtGQf19rY1

Artificial intelligence is increasingly disrupting our economy, contributing to layoffs and occupational changes. [...] This bill allows us to remain proactive, protect workers who are most impacted by the technology, and supercharge the future of work by ensuring our future workforce has the skills they need to succeed.

The development of data centers is rapidly increasing across the country, and there is legitimate concern about how these projects could raise utility bills, harm our environment, or impact public health.

As your Senator, I’m doing everything I can to make sure young people are prepared for the workforce of the future.

From job training and investment to shaping AI regulations, I’ll keep working to support Delaware's workers today and tomorrow.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh wants to gamble with America's workforce in the era of AI.
 
I'm not willing to make decisions that impact our workers and economic stability based on a bet. https://t.co/oOfbS7x8i7

AI innovation cannot come at the expense of Americans’ safety and security. 

After reports of AI systems accessing real-world networks without authorization, I’m demanding answers from @OpenAI and @AnthropicAI. 

Congress needs the facts. And the American people need strong safeguards, now.

https://t.co/4sOO7vWGro

Recent “autonomous hackings” show there’s still so much we don’t know about AI.

We need to hold these companies accountable as we continue to explore the unknown.
https://t.co/pWMasGxiiZ

As AI models advance, so should safety and oversight practices, but recent hacking incidents show these companies should be doing more.

I pressed OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta for answers on how they’ll keep our communities safe. https://t.co/bblU2QlK8O

Even if there was a 1% chance AI could wipe out human life, we should be pumping the brakes to make sure we have the proper safeguards in place, not racing blindly into disaster.

It's time for Congress to step in and find the balance between safety and innovation, before it's too late.

It's time for AI CEOs to come to Congress for immediate public hearings so the American public know the risks of this AI frontier.

This moment requires bipartisan action. That's why @SenJohnCurtis and I are calling on @SenateCommerce to set a hearing— we can't afford to wait. https://t.co/T35yGCkD0t

AI is out of control and the American people deserve answers. 

It's time bring these CEOs to Washington for a hearing in @senatecommerce. https://t.co/cpQwkHxfP9

Almost every week there’s a new report on the growing capabilities of artificial intelligence (AI), and like many of you, I’ve been laser-focused on these headlines. While this technology offers opportunities for our economy, our health, and the potential to solve some of the most challenging problems, experts continue to highlight risks and are urgently calling for us to guard against unintended consequences.
How worried should we be about AI? Let's ask. https://t.co/AY9XICkuyz

The AI race is out of control and our president is rambling on about how we talk about it.

Call it whatever you want, but we need to start taking these threats seriously. https://t.co/Z4VS2mc88H

AI is becoming more unrecognizable by the day, and now scammers are using it to take advantage of Americans – especially older Americans – across the country.

My AI Fraud Accountability Act will ban fraudsters from using these realistic AI impersonations to rip you off.
https://t.co/ZFtsRWJUWc

There’s still much more to do.

It’s time for leading AI companies to come before Congress and explain to the American people what’s happening and how they’ll keep us safe as this technology evolves. https://t.co/eDk4eBMw5J

With more Americans using AI every day, we need to do all we can to cut down on AI-related fraud. [...] Our AI Fraud Accountability Act would ensure our statutes are updated to meet this current moment.

Analysis from the National Partnership for Women and Families found that women make up over half of workers that are in the most AI-vulnerable occupations, with women of color making up nearly a third of workers in AI-vulnerable jobs. Dr. Heck, in your testimony, you focus on worker mobility. What can you share with us about how the economic mobility of women and people of color in the workforce might be impacted by AI.

Many news reports have come out about new entrants into the workforce, whether it’s college students, women, and people of color disproportionately being impacted by or exposed to occupations most vulnerable to AI. I’m concerned that AI is moving much faster than we are, and we’re not taking advantage of the disruptions or the opportunities. If you could pick one or two workforce indicators that Congress should be closely watching, what would they be?
